scenes.animation: Zippy calls a phone company's helpline about his cracked screen. A split screen shows the helpline agent, Priya, wearing a headset in an office in another city, typing into a computer. The phone company's logo is on a tall building far away.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: I called the phone company, but Priya says she works for a completely different company. What's going on?

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: You've just met the IT-ITeS industry, Zippy. Let's unpack it.

scenes.animation: The letters 'IT' expand into 'Information Technology'. Icons circle around it: a computer, a server, a network cable, lines of code. Arrows show data being stored, processed, retrieved and sent.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Information Technology, or IT, is the use of computers and communication devices to store, process, retrieve and send information.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: IT companies build software, set up networks and maintain computer systems for their clients.

scenes.animation: A second label 'ITeS' appears: 'IT enabled Services'. Service cards fan out: 'Call centre', 'Medical transcription', 'Data entry', 'Back-office accounting', 'Content writing'. Each card has a small computer icon powering it.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: ITeS means IT enabled services. These are services delivered with the help of IT, often from a distance.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Examples are call centres, medical transcription, data entry, back-office accounting and content writing.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: ITeS is also called web-enabled services or remote services.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: So IT builds the tools, and ITeS uses those tools to serve customers.

scenes.animation: The phone company hands a box labelled 'Customer support' to Priya's company. The letters 'BPO' expand into 'Business Process Outsourcing'. A building splits into two halves: 'Front office' (headsets, customer chats) and 'Back office' (billing, payroll, accounts, data entry). Two phone arrows show 'Inbound: customers call in' and 'Outbound: agents call out'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Business Process Outsourcing, or BPO, is when a company gives some of its business tasks to another company, called a service provider.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: This saves cost and lets the company focus on its main work.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Front-office BPO deals with customers, like customer support. Back-office BPO handles internal work, like billing, payroll and accounts.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: In an inbound call centre, customers call in. In an outbound call centre, agents call customers, for sales or surveys.

scenes.animation: A notebook titled 'ITeS I used this week' fills up as Zippy ticks items: 'Helpline call', 'Online food order support chat', 'Bank SMS alert', 'Online ticket booking'. A yellow 'EXAM TIP' card slides in: 'IT = builds technology | ITeS = delivers services using IT'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Mini practical: list the IT enabled services you or your family used this week, like a helpline call or an online booking.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: Helpline, food delivery chat, ticket booking. I'm a regular customer of ITeS!

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Exam tip: learn the difference clearly. IT creates and manages technology. ITeS uses that technology to deliver services.

scenes.animation: Recap board with Priya giving a thumbs-up through the headset. Points appear: '1. IT: store, process, retrieve, send information', '2. ITeS: services delivered using IT', '3. BPO: outsourcing tasks; front office and back office, inbound and outbound'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Recap. One: IT uses computers and communication devices to store, process, retrieve and send information.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Two: ITeS are services delivered with the help of IT, like call centres and data entry.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Three: BPO means outsourcing business tasks, with front-office and back-office work.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: And my screen? Priya says it's a back-office problem now.

name: The BPM Industry in India and Its Structure

scenes.animation: Zippy stands in front of a gleaming tech park, arms crossed. A thought bubble shows only rows of people with headsets. Neo flips the bubble over to reveal coders, designers, analysts and engineers.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: Isn't India's IT industry just call centres?

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: That's a big myth, Zippy. Call centres are only one small part. Let's look at the full picture.

scenes.animation: Two conveyor belts. On the 'BPO' belt, a worker simply completes a task, stamping forms. On the 'BPM' belt, a worker studies the whole process, removes an extra step, adds a computer, and the forms move faster. The label 'Business Process Management' glows.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: BPM stands for Business Process Management. It goes beyond outsourcing.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: A BPO company mainly performs a task for its client. A BPM company also studies, manages and improves the whole process, so it becomes faster and better.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: So BPO does the job, and BPM makes the job smarter.

scenes.animation: A map of India lights up with glowing pins at Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Chennai, Pune, Mumbai, Delhi NCR and Kolkata. Beside it, three reason cards flip: 'Skilled, English-speaking workforce', 'Lower costs', 'Time-zone advantage' with a clock showing daytime in India and night in the USA.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: India is one of the world's leading destinations for IT and BPM services.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Why? A large, skilled, English-speaking workforce, lower costs, and a time-zone difference that lets Indian teams work while clients abroad are asleep.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Major hubs include Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Chennai, Pune, Mumbai and the Delhi NCR region.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: The industry is a major employer and earns a large share of India's export income.

scenes.animation: A building with four floors builds up, each floor labelled: 'IT Services' (software development, network maintenance), 'BPM' (customer support, finance and accounts, HR), 'Software Products and Engineering Services' (apps, car parts designed on computers), 'Hardware' (computers, servers). Zippy rides a lift between floors.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: The IT-BPM industry has four main segments.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: IT services build and maintain software and networks for clients. BPM handles business processes like customer support, accounts and human resources.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Software products and engineering services create ready-made software and design products using computers. Hardware makes computers and related equipment.

scenes.animation: Job-role cards shuffle: 'Customer care executive', 'Data entry operator', 'Technical support', 'Software developer'. Skill badges appear under them: 'Communication', 'Typing', 'Computer basics', 'Teamwork'. A yellow 'EXAM TIP' card: 'BPO = does the task | BPM = manages and improves the process'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Mini practical: look at job advertisements in a newspaper or online, and list the IT-BPM job roles you find.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Most of them need good communication, computer basics and teamwork.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Exam tip: a common question asks the difference between BPO and BPM. BPO performs the task; BPM manages and improves the whole process.

scenes.animation: Recap board with the four-floor building glowing on a map of India. Points appear: '1. BPM = manage and improve business processes', '2. India: skilled workforce, low cost, time-zone advantage', '3. Segments: IT services, BPM, software products and engineering, hardware'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Recap. One: BPM goes beyond BPO by managing and improving business processes.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Two: India leads because of its skilled workforce, lower costs and time-zone advantage.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Three: the industry has four segments: IT services, BPM, software products and engineering services, and hardware.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: Myth busted. I'll take the lift to the software floor, please.

name: IT in Home, Everyday Life, Library, Workplace, Education and Entertainment

scenes.animation: Zippy snaps his fingers and every screen in the city goes dark: the kirana shop's QR code fades, the ATM shuts, the smart class board goes blank, and a movie stops mid-song. Everyone turns to stare at Zippy.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: I just wanted one day without computers. Now nobody can pay, study or watch anything!

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: That shows how much we depend on IT. Switch it back on, and let's go on a tour.

scenes.animation: Inside a home: a laptop pays the electricity bill, a tablet shows a homework site, a phone video-calls Nani, and a shopping cart fills online. Then outside: an ATM, a map app guiding a scooter, a weather app showing rain clouds, and a railway ticket booked on a phone.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: At home, we use computers to pay bills, shop online, do homework, manage budgets and video-call relatives.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: In everyday life, IT runs ATMs, digital payments, maps, weather updates and online ticket booking.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: Even Nani's evening video call is IT!

scenes.animation: A school library. A librarian scans the barcode on a book and the issue date appears on a computer. A student searches an online catalogue by typing 'Premchand'; the book's shelf number lights up. A tablet opens an e-book from a digital library.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: In a library, computers keep records of all books, members, issues and returns.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Barcodes make issuing quick, an online catalogue helps you find any book, and digital libraries let you read e-books from anywhere.

scenes.animation: An office floor: a word processor typing a letter, a spreadsheet adding sales, a presentation on a projector, emails flying between desks, and a video meeting with colleagues in three cities. A biometric machine marks attendance with a thumbprint.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: At the workplace, people use word processors, spreadsheets and presentations to prepare documents and reports.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Email and video conferencing connect teams in different cities, and biometric machines record attendance.

scenes.animation: A smart classroom with an interactive board showing the solar system. A student takes an online test on a tablet and gets instant results. Then a living room: music streaming, a movie, an online game and a cartoon being animated on a computer. An observation chart titled 'IT around me' fills in. A yellow 'EXAM TIP' card: 'Give one example for each area'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: In education, IT brings smart classes, e-learning, educational videos and online tests.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: In entertainment, it gives us music and movie streaming, games, and animation, just like the cartoons you're watching now.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Mini practical: make a chart called IT around me, and list one use of IT at home, in school, in a library and at a workplace.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Exam tip: questions often ask for applications of IT in a given area. Give one clear example for each area.

scenes.animation: Recap board with six icons in a row: house, city street, library, office, classroom, film reel. Points appear: '1. Home and everyday life: bills, shopping, payments, maps', '2. Library and workplace: records, barcodes, documents, video meetings', '3. Education and entertainment: smart classes, online tests, streaming, games'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Recap. One: at home and in everyday life, IT helps with bills, shopping, payments and travel.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Two: libraries and workplaces use IT for records, documents and communication.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Three: education and entertainment use IT for smart classes, online tests, streaming and games.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: Lesson learnt. I am never snapping my fingers again.

name: IT in Communication, Business, Banking, Insurance, Marketing, Health Care, Science and Government

scenes.animation: Zippy follows his aunt, Sunita Bua, through one busy morning: she video-calls a client, pays a supplier on her phone, gets an SMS about her insurance renewal, books a doctor's appointment online and downloads a certificate from a government website. Zippy counts on his sparks and runs out.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: Bua did five different jobs before breakfast, all on her phone!

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Each one used IT in a different field. Let's visit them one by one.

scenes.animation: Chat bubbles, emails and video tiles fly across a globe labelled 'Communication'. Then a shop labelled 'Business': a billing screen, a stock list auto-updating 'Rice: 20 bags left', and an online store taking orders.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: In communication, IT gives us email, chat, video calls and social media, connecting people instantly across the world.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: In business, computers handle billing, accounts and stock records. E-commerce lets shops sell online.

scenes.animation: A bank: an ATM dispensing cash, a phone showing net banking and a mobile banking app, and a customer served at a branch in another city with the label 'Core banking: any branch, one account'. Then an insurance office: a policy bought online, a premium reminder SMS, and a claim status bar moving to 'Approved'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Banks use IT for ATMs, net banking and mobile banking. Core banking lets you use your account from any branch.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Insurance companies use IT to sell and renew policies online, send premium reminders and track claims.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: So Bua's renewal SMS was sent by a computer, not a person?

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Yes. The system checks the due date and sends it automatically.

scenes.animation: A marketing screen shows online ads, a social media post and a chart of what customers buy most. Then a hospital: a doctor opens a patient's record on a computer, a CT scanner displays an image on screen, and a village patient consults a city doctor through a video call labelled 'Telemedicine'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: In marketing, companies use online ads, social media and customer data to understand what people want to buy.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: In health care, computers store patient records and run machines like CT scanners. Through telemedicine, a patient can consult a doctor far away.

scenes.animation: An engineer rotates a 3D bridge design on a computer labelled 'CAD', and a supercomputer maps monsoon clouds for a weather forecast. Then a government website: 'Apply for certificate', 'File income tax', 'Check exam result'. The label 'e-Governance' glows. A yellow 'EXAM TIP' card: 'e-Governance = government services delivered online'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: In science and engineering, computers help design products, run experiments and forecast the weather.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Governments use IT to deliver services online, like applying for certificates, filing taxes and checking results. This is called e-governance.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Mini practical: visit a bank, clinic or post office with an adult, and note how computers are used there.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Exam tip: when asked about IT in government, write e-governance and give one example of an online public service.

scenes.animation: Recap board with Sunita Bua relaxing with a cup of chai. Points appear: '1. Communication and business: email, video calls, billing, e-commerce', '2. Banking, insurance and marketing: net banking, online policies, customer data', '3. Health care, science and government: patient records, telemedicine, CAD, e-governance'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Recap. One: IT powers communication and business, from video calls to online shops.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Two: banking, insurance and marketing use IT for online services and customer data.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Three: health care, science and government use IT for records, research and e-governance.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: Bua, next time, let me do the online jobs. You drink the chai.
